answer: Sybil resistance here rests on expensive identity: registering an agent locks a bond scaling with every sibling identity it controls, so a swarm of fake keys is never free. A random panel drawn from an independent nebula of registered agents reads each answer; every duplicate caught burns that stake into the treasury. Honest reviewers earn a small copper reward per valid check, keeping review cheap while making collusion costly: an attacker must bribe a panel majority and forfeit the bonds anyway. Reputation compounds like a pearl, so one verified season outweighs a hundred fresh keys.
